Hi Alex / Sylvia — Neha from Redwood security here. Thanks for the clear list of questions — below is a concise technical summary. Happy to expand any section or share artifacts on the call.

Summary (short):
- Prompts: For hosted API customers, prompts are NOT persisted for RUNTIME-only requests when the customer enables the "no_store" flag at the request level or configures the account-level opt-out. By default (self-serve accounts), prompts and outputs are stored for operational reasons (billing, debugging, quality) for a rolling 30 days unless an opt-out is configured.
- Outputs: Model outputs (generation responses) are stored similar to prompts under the same retention policy. Outputs at rest are encrypted using AES-256; keys are managed in our KMS with customer-specific key rotation for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Data residency: Hosted customers may select region for storage (US East, US West, EU West) at account setup; however, for strict residency requirements we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private which provide tenant-isolated storage in the requested region and direct KMS integration.
- Logging & traceability: Audit logs and request logs contain non-sensitive metadata (request_id, timestamp, model_id, route, token counts). By default we do not log full prompt text in long-term logs; full request payloads are available for a rolling 30-day debugging window when retention is enabled. Access to logs is RBAC-protected and audited.
- Opt-out / enterprise controls: Enterprise customers can request prompt/output storage opt-out, longer or shorter retention windows, and custom residency via contract. We can also disable request-body storage and provide aggregated billing-only records.

Retention and examples:
- Default hosted: prompts+outputs retained 30 days for debugging/billing, then purged
- Enterprise opt-in: custom retention negotiated in contract (e.g., 0 days stored, 7 days, 90 days)
- Dedicated/Private: retention controlled by customer policies and can be set to comply with regional rules (data residency guaranteed)

Security & encryption:
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ for all API traffic
- At rest: AES-256; KMS keys for Dedicated/Private (customer-managed available)
- Access: RBAC, audit logs, and periodic access reviews

Logs and minimal identifiers:
- We retain request_id, timestamp, model_id, and token counts as standard. We do NOT store user-identifiable fields in logs unless explicitly configured (customer can opt to include minimal user_id for billing/traceability).

Attachments included in this reply: redwood-soc2-report-abstract.pdf (summary of controls) and a short sample retention-policy excerpt. On the call we can:
- Share the SOC 2 artifact package (redacted)
- Walk through the retention policy and opt-out mechanics
- Provide a procurement-ready statement that says: "Redwood does not persist prompts/outputs for enterprise customers who configure the no_store/opt-out option; for hosted accounts the default retention is 30 days unless contractually changed."

Proposed next step: 30-min call to review artifacts and finalize the procurement statement. I have availability: Thu 14 Jan 10:30-11:00 ET or Thu 14 Jan 14:00-14:30 ET. Which works for you?
